We have to decide what promotes dignity, freedom, mutual care, and sustainable flourishing. We have to decide what kind of world we are building and who pays the price for the values we normalize. And the basis for that shared work is not sectarian doctrine. It is our shared biological and social reality. We are vulnerable creatures. We can be wounded, deprived, manipulated, and excluded. We can also be nurtured, protected, liberated, and empowered. That common condition gives us a real basis for common ethics. Not because everyone will agree on everything, but because everyone is living inside the same basic moral universe of harm, need, relationship, and consequence.
